source_text: Quid est, quod "in Iudaeorum superbiam" frustra conaris "ista verba transferre, tamquam ipsos in se transfiguraverit Apostolus, qui contemnebant dona Christi, velut sibi non necessaria"? Sic enim suspicaris: … Sed ideo dicis a Iudaeis fuisse contempta, "quod veniam daret ille peccatis, quae ipsi legis admonitione vitassent".
pass_a_gloss: What is it that 'onto the pride of the Jews' you vainly try 'to transfer these words, as if the Apostle transfigured into himself those who despised the gifts of Christ, as not necessary to themselves'? For so you suspect. But for this reason you say (they) were despised by the Jews, 'because he gave pardon to sins which they themselves by the admonition of the law had avoided'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Why do you try in vain ‘to transfer these words to the pride of the Jews, as though the Apostle had represented in himself those who despised the gifts of Christ as not necessary for them’? For that is your conjecture. … But you say that they were despised by the Jews for this reason, ‘that he gave pardon for sins which they themselves had avoided through the admonition of the law.’”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
